TX

Excise Taxes & Federal Compliance

Trucking carriers face a web of federal and state excise tax obligations that change with mileage, weight, routes, and fuel consumption. Missing a Form 2290 filing, IFTA quarterly report, or IRP renewal can ground your fleet. BOF tracks every obligation, deadline, and filing status so nothing slips.

  • Form 2290 / HVUT filing and stamped Schedule 1 tracking
  • IFTA quarterly fuel tax reporting across all jurisdictions
  • IRP apportioned registration and cab card management
  • UCR annual registration and state weight-distance tax compliance
Explore Excise Taxes →
AC

Accounting & Financial Operations

Trucking accounting requires per-mile cost tracking, load-level profitability, factoring reconciliation, and driver settlement accounting that general-purpose platforms do not handle cleanly. BOF structures your financials around how freight actually moves. Your books reflect your lanes, not just your bank account.

  • Trucking-specific chart of accounts for revenue, fuel, maintenance, and driver pay
  • Load-level and lane-level P&L visibility
  • Factoring reconciliation and advance tracking
  • AP for fuel cards, vendor invoices, and owner-operator settlements
Explore Accounting →
ER

ERP & Workflow Integration

Enterprise Resource Planning for a fleet means connecting dispatch, maintenance, compliance, and finance so handoffs do not fall through the gaps between departments. BOF creates visible queues, named owners, due dates, and operational consequences for every administrative task.

  • Load-to-cash workflow automation from dispatch through invoice
  • Asset lifecycle management for tractors, trailers, and equipment
  • Vendor and supplier management with renewal tracking
  • Cross-department task queues with assignment and escalation
Explore ERP →
HR

Human Resources & DOT Compliance

Hiring, onboarding, and managing CDL drivers is a DOT-regulated function where every personnel file must contain specific documentation. BOF manages the compliance layer your HR platform was never built for, including DQF, drug and alcohol program records, medical cards, MVRs, and Clearinghouse queries.

  • Driver Qualification File assembly and ongoing monitoring
  • DOT drug and alcohol program tracking
  • CDL, medical certificate, and license expiration alerts
  • New hire onboarding workflows tied to dispatch readiness
Explore HR →
PY

Payroll & Driver Compensation

Trucking payroll may include per-mile, percentage-of-load, hourly, day-rate, and 1099 owner-operator structures inside the same fleet. BOF helps the office connect compensation rules, load data, deductions, per-diem, and settlement evidence before payroll questions become driver disputes.

  • Per-mile, percentage, hourly, day-rate, and 1099 pay models
  • Multi-state withholding and nexus issue visibility
  • Driver per-diem, deductions, and escrow tracking
  • Payroll-to-settlement reconciliation tied to load data

Operational integration

Every issue needs a reason, owner, due date, operational consequence, and clearance path.

Administrative data only matters when it changes a fleet decision. BOF keeps the office record tied to what operations can release, hold, pay, bill, or escalate.

Reason

Why is the item not ready?

Missing W-9, payroll setup gap, tax support, stale vendor approval, unmatched receipt, or unresolved benefits issue.

Owner

Who owns the next action?

HR owner, payroll desk, finance lead, AP reviewer, vendor manager, or BOF support path is named before work drifts.

Consequence

What fleet decision is affected?

Driver readiness, vendor use, settlement release, customer billing, cash-flow forecast, or leadership review.

Clearance

What clears the hold?

The record shows the document, approval, policy step, payment check, or service support required to move forward.
